questions.answer: It was ok but the bureaucracy of the UW administration was unnecessary and kafkaesque.

questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That NO information was given that you had to pay for your own kitchen appliances. Now, they are just back in Poland.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I'm glad that I lived in a modern student dorm (although, it was ridiculous and an invasion of the privacy that we had to sleep to people in each room) but the older ones were not of a quality appropriate to students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very bureaucratic

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: For example, getting the photo for the student card was extremely hard to get approved and there was very little flexibility of the administration to take regard of your personal situation. I experienced that they were very inflexible with regards to taking a Polish language course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email and appointments

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare to be frustrated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some professors took no or little regard to the description of the course in the catalogue, most classes used no academic litterature, sometimes the professor just talked for three hours without any notes, powerpoints etc., and the lack of laptops in any part of the courses made it seem like a third degree programme.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took both but the quality didn't vary.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was of an extremely low quality, not suited for a serious degree at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Prepare for bureaucracy
2) Sociale with Poles and learn the language
3) Use money on fun things

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *

questions.answer: The experiences
